                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ruction of the Jews, or in his Glory at the last Day, the Afflictions specified are, <ns0:hi>A being hated of all Nations, de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />livered up to Councils; beating in the Synagogues, casting into Prisons, and being Killed.</ns0:hi> All which happened to the Disciples of Christ before the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> The Christians were counted a <ns0:hi>Sect every where spoken against, Acts</ns0:hi> 28.22. <ns0:hi>Stephen</ns0:hi> was stoned, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 7.29. <ns0:hi>Iames</ns0:hi> was kil<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />led with the sword, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 12.2. <ns0:hi>Paul and Silas</ns0:hi> were im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />prisoned, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 16.23. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> five <ns0:hi>times received of the Iews forty stripes save one,</ns0:hi> he was <ns0:hi>thrice beaten with Rods,</ns0:hi> once <ns0:hi>Stoned.</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 11.24, 25. He was brought before <ns0:hi>King Agrippa,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Festus, Peter</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> were call'd be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the <ns0:hi>Council. Acts Ch.</ns0:hi> 4.7. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 5.21. so as all these things hap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pened before the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and this may be interpreted as a sign of that great Destruction but not of that only, for the Text saith, you shall be <ns0:hi>hated of all Nations,</ns0:hi> which came to pass afterward, when Christianity was perse<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cuted by Heathens for three hundred years together, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, this should be done for <ns0:hi>a Testimony against them.</ns0:hi> That is, the Persecutors. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>it shall turn to you for a Te<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stimony.</ns0:hi> The Persecutions of Christians are. 1. A <ns0:hi>Testi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mony against the Persecutors,</ns0:hi> of their Ingratitude, and Cru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />elty, and Hatred to the Name of Christ. 2. They are a <ns0:hi>Testimony to the Persecuted,</ns0:hi> of their Faith, and Patience, and Courage, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 And then shall many be offended, and shall be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tray one another, and shall hate one another.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith. <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.12, 13. <ns0:hi>The Brother shall betray the Brother to Death, and the Father the Son, and Children shall rise up against their Parents, and cause them to be put to Death. And you shall be hated of all Men for my Names sake. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.16. <ns0:hi>And you shall be betrayed, both by Parents, and Brethren, and Kins-folk, and Friends, and some of you shall they accuse to be put to Death. And you shall be hated of all Men for my Names sake. Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny shall be offended.</ns0:hi> The meaning is, shall turn Apostates, stumbling at these great Afflictions, and <ns0:hi>Persecutions</ns0:hi> for the Gospel. <ns0:hi>And shall betray one anther.</ns0:hi> We Read of several Apostates in holy Writ, such as <ns0:hi>Phigellus, Hermogenes, De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mas, Hymeneus, Philetus,</ns0:hi> and others; but all things not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Written that were done, we have no particular <ns0:hi>Record</ns0:hi> of such <ns0:hi>Treachery,</ns0:hi> as is here mentioned. But it is no other than we may reasonably presume was done, tho we had not been assured of it, to justify our Saviours Prediction. There is no time of great <ns0:hi>Persecution,</ns0:hi> but proves a time of <ns0:hi>great Aposta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cy</ns0:hi> and some <ns0:hi>Treachery.</ns0:hi> It hath been a constant observation, that no hatred flames to that degree, with hatred upon the account of <ns0:hi>Religion.</ns0:hi> Nor is what our Saviour here pre dicted more, than the History of all Ages of the Church have justifyed.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:263" />11 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Pet. 2.1.</ns0:note> many false prophets shall arise, and shall deceive many.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.<ns0:note place="bottom">Here are two Signs more given. 1. <ns0:hi>The abounding of false Teachers.</ns0:hi> 2. <ns0:hi>The Abatements of Christians Zeal, and love to God.</ns0:hi> For the matter of the 11. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> we shall meet with it more fully, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 23, 24. By the <ns0:hi>aboundings of Iniquity</ns0:hi> here, we may either understand, the <ns0:hi>Rage</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Malice,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cruelty</ns0:hi> of the Enemies of the Gospel, or, 2. The <ns0:hi>Apostacy</ns0:hi> of such as are professors. Both these are great Temptations, and tho they will not Extinguish that Holy Fire which God hath kindled in good Souls, yet they have oft times a very ill influ<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ence upon them to abate of their former warmth in the ways of God. Or if we understand it of <ns0:hi>Love to Brethren,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />postacy</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Professors</ns0:hi> much cooleth the Christian, not know<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing who they may trust, and confide in as sincere. If by the abounding of Iniquity, we understand the abounding of <ns0:hi>Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fanness</ns0:hi> in the General (which always also aboundeth most in times of Persecution) that also hath no small Influence up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on Christians warmth in their Profession, to cool and abate it. <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 10.25. 2 <ns0:hi>Tim,</ns0:hi> 1.15. & 4.16.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 But he that shall indure to the end, the same shall be saved.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have the same, <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 13.13. We also met with it before, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 10.22. It is a promise to Perseverence, especial<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ly to such Perseverance as is joyned with Fortitude, He that shall not be tempted to Apostacy through the Afflictions of the Gospel, but shall patiently and Courageously indure all the sufferings which shall follow the Profession of the Gospel, <ns0:hi>shall be saved,</ns0:hi> if not preserved and so saved with a Tempo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral Salvation, yet he shall be <ns0:hi>Eternally</ns0:hi> saved.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 And this gospel of the kingdom, shall be preached in all the world, for a witness unto all na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions, and then shall the end come.<ns0:note place="bottom">So saith <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.10. some think that <ns0:hi>the end</ns0:hi> men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tioned in the Close of this Verse, refers to the <ns0:hi>Destruction of Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> others, that it referreth to <ns0:hi>the Day of Iudgment.</ns0:hi> If we take World (as it is often taken) for the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> in opposition to the Jews, <ns0:hi>Synechdochically,</ns0:hi> the whole being put for a great part; it is most certain, that before <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> was destroyed, the <ns0:hi>Gospel</ns0:hi> which is here called the Gospel of the Kingdom, either because it shews the way to the Kingdom of God, or because it is that sacred Instrument, by which Christ subdueth Mens Hearts to himself, was preached to the World, that is, to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> and that to a great part of them. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> alone had carried it from <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Illyricum.</ns0:hi> The Ro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mans Faith was spoken of throughout the World, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 1.8. <ns0:hi>Paul Col.</ns0:hi> 1.23. saith it was preached to <ns0:hi>every Creature,</ns0:hi> see also, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 10.16. & 15, 16<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Col.</ns0:hi> 1.6. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 3.16. But o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />thers chuse by <ns0:hi>the end</ns0:hi> here to understand the <ns0:hi>End of the World.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 When ye therefore shall see the abomina<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of desolation spoken of by Daniel the pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phet, stand in the holy place, (who so readeth let him understand.)<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> saith, <ns0:hi>Standing where it ought not.</ns0:hi> Here are two Questions. 1. <ns0:hi>What is here meant by the Abo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mination of Desolations.</ns0:hi> 2. What Text in <ns0:hi>Daniel our Lord referreth to.</ns0:hi> As to the latter, there are three places in <ns0:hi>Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />niel</ns0:hi> which mention it, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 9.27. <ns0:hi>for the over-spreading of Abominations,</ns0:hi> or (as it is in the <ns0:hi>Margent</ns0:hi>) with the <ns0:hi>A<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bominable Armies i. e. shall make it desolate, Ch.</ns0:hi> 11.31. <ns0:hi>They shall place the Abomination that maketh desolate, Ch.</ns0:hi> 12, 11. <ns0:hi>From the time that the daily Sacrifice shall be ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken away, and the Abomination that maketh desolate, set up.</ns0:hi> Mr. <ns0:hi>Calvin</ns0:hi> thinks that the Text in <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> here referred to, is that <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 12.11. others say, that it is that <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 9.27. contending that those two other Texts speak of <ns0:hi>Antiochus,</ns0:hi> which is the very Reason given by others to the contrary. It is of no great Consequence to us to know which Verse our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour referreth to. Be it which it would, it was spoken of by <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Prophet,</ns0:hi> by which Quotation our Saviour doth both give his <ns0:hi>Testimony</ns0:hi> to that Book, as a part of <ns0:hi>Holy Writ,</ns0:hi> and also lets his Disciples know, that what he told them, was but what was prophesied of, and so must have its Accomplishment, and that the <ns0:hi>Iewish Worship</ns0:hi> was to cease. As to the second Question amidst the great Variety of Notions about it, I take theirs to be the best who understand the <ns0:hi>Abomination of Dissolations,</ns0:hi> to be meant of the <ns0:hi>Roman Armies,</ns0:hi> which being made up of Idolatrous Souldiers, and having with them many <ns0:hi>Abominable Images,</ns0:hi> are therefore called the <ns0:hi>Abomination</ns0:hi>; those Words of <ns0:hi>Desolations</ns0:hi> are ad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ded, because they were to make <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> desolate, and so St. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> who hath not these Words, possibly gives us in o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther Words, the best Interpretation of them, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 21.20. <ns0:hi>And when you shall see Ierusalem compassed with Armies, then know that the Desolation thereof is nigh.</ns0:hi> When saith our Lord, you shall see the <ns0:hi>Abominable Armies stand in the holy place,</ns0:hi> that is upon the holy Ground (as all <ns0:hi>Iudea</ns0:hi> was) whoso readeth those Prophesies of the Prophet <ns0:hi>Daniel [let him understand]</ns0:hi> that as through the Righte<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous Judgment of God, he once suffered the <ns0:hi>holy place</ns0:hi> to be polluted by the Abominable Armies of <ns0:hi>Antiochus,</ns0:hi> which he foretold, so he will again suffer the <ns0:hi>holy place</ns0:hi> to be Pollu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ted by the <ns0:hi>Abominable Armies of the Romans,</ns0:hi> who shall make the holy place desolate, which was Prophesied by the Prophet <ns0:hi>Daniel,</ns0:hi> as well as the former. Therefore saith our Saviour, when you see the Roman Armies pitch their Tents before <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> be you then assured, God will give <ns0:hi>Ieru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem</ns0:hi> into their Hands, and then all that I have foretold, shall come to pass.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Then let them which be in Judea, flee into the mountains.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Let him which is on the house top, not come down to take any thing out of his house.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 Neither let him which is in the field, return back to take his cloths.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath this, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13, 14, 15, 16. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.21. <ns0:hi>Then let them that are in</ns0:hi> Judea <ns0:hi>Flee to the Mountains, and let them which are in the midst of it, depart out, and let not them that are in the Countries enter thereinto.</ns0:hi> The import of all this, is no more than, Let every Man with as much speed as he can, shift for himself, for as <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith. Then the Desolation of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> is nigh; for as he addeth, <ns0:hi>These are the Days of Vengeance, that all things which are Written may be fulfilled.</ns0:hi> Let none of you think the Storm will over, for when you see this, be assured the time is come, when all I have spoken of this City, shall be accomplish<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 And woe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith nothing of the <ns0:hi>Sabbath day, Ch.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath not what <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> hath, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. <ns0:hi>Woe to them</ns0:hi> in this Text, is only a Phrase testifying our Saviours Compassion on such, and indicative of the addition it would make to their Misery, as it would retard their Flight. Upon this account also, he bids them pray <ns0:hi>their Flight might not be in the Win<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter, neither on the Sabbath day.</ns0:hi> The Winter would Na<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />turally retard their motion, through the cold, and moisture of it. The <ns0:hi>Sabbath</ns0:hi> would be a <ns0:hi>Moral hindrance</ns0:hi> in regard of the Superstitious opinion they had of the Sabbath, that they might not upon that Day defend themselves, nor Flee from their Enemies beyond the length of a <ns0:hi>Sabbath Days Iourney,</ns0:hi> which was but two Miles, our Saviour hinteth them, that their Flight must be further. When our Saviour spake this, the <ns0:hi>Iewish Sabbath</ns0:hi> was the Day of holy Rest, and he knew that altho by his Resurrection, he should Sanctify a <ns0:hi>new Sabbath,</ns0:hi> yet the Jews would not for a time understand that the old <ns0:hi>Sabbath</ns0:hi> was Abolished. Here is therefore no Establishment of the old <ns0:hi>Sabbath,</ns0:hi> to be observed after his <ns0:hi>Resurrection</ns0:hi>; The praying that their Flight might not be upon the <ns0:hi>Sabbath Day</ns0:hi> respected only either their <ns0:hi>remora</ns0:hi> to their Flight, which the Sabbath would give them (in case they should keep it as an Holy Rest) or the addition of trouble it would make in their Spirits, when they considered that was the Day in which they were wont to go to the house of Prayer, keeping it a Day of Holy Rest unto God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Dan. 12.1.</ns0:note> then shall be great tribulation such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no nor ever shall be.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 And except those days should be shortned, there should no flesh be saved, but for the elects sake, those days shall be shortned.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the same in effect, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 19, 20. <ns0:hi>Luke Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.23, 24. speaks more particularly. <ns0:hi>For there shall be great distress in the Land, and wrath upon this People. And they shall fall by the Edge of the Sword, and shall be led away Captive into all Nations; and Ierusa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lem shall be <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>roden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled.</ns0:hi> These Verses must be understood with reference to the <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> Nation, and whoso shall read in <ns0:hi>Iosephus,</ns0:hi> the History of the <ns0:hi>Wars of the Iews,</ns0:hi> will easily agree, there is nothing in all the foregoing <ns0:hi>Iewish</ns0:hi> story, which we have recorded in Scripture like unto it, the final De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction of them by <ns0:hi>Titus,</ns0:hi> was rather an abatement of Miseries, they suffered by the Factions within themselves than any thing else. And thus some think, that God shortned those days of their Misery, by sending the <ns0:hi>Roman Armies</ns0:hi> to quiet the Seditions, and Factions amongst themselves, which were more cruel one to another; God promiseth to shorten these days for the Elect sake, that were amongst this sinful People. So that as the City was taken in less than six Months, so was their whole Country, in less than eighteen Months more: And if the Lord had not in Compassion to those amongst this People, who belonged to his Election of Grace, shortned these days of Calamity, both by sending the <ns0:hi>Roman Armies,</ns0:hi> to quiet their intestine Divisions, and then giving these Armies so quick a Victory, none of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> would have been le<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t alive, which indeed any one will judge, that shall but read those Histories.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:264" />23 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 17.33 <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 21.8.</ns0:note> Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo here <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> Christ, or there, believe <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> not.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Deu. 13.1. 2 Thes. 2.11.</ns0:note> there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders insomuch that if <ns0:hi>it were</ns0:hi> possible they shall deceive the very elect.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Behold, I have told you before.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hold he is in the desert, go not forth, Behold <ns0:hi>he is</ns0:hi> in the secret chambers, believe <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> not.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.21, 22, 23. There is no doubt, but that our Saviour here hath a special Respect to those Persons, who about the time of the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> taking advantage of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Expectation</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Messiah.</ns0:hi> as a secular Prince, who should restore them to Liberty (an Opinion, which as we have often heard had infected the Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nerality of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; and not a little even the Disciples of Christ) made themselves Heads of Parties, and pretended that they were the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Christ,</ns0:hi> thereby to incourage People to follow them, and to stand up for their Liberty, of which kind there were several mentioned both in the History of <ns0:hi>Iosep<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>us,</ns0:hi> and in the <ns0:hi>Roman History,</ns0:hi> respecting those times Our Lord therefore cautioneth his Disciples against such, and thereby taketh them off their Expectation of any such secular Kingdom of the <ns0:hi>Messiah,</ns0:hi> as they had dreamed of. He tells them, that there would such Persons arise, and some of them should do great signs and wonders, insomuch that if it were possible, they would deceive <ns0:hi>the Elect of God,</ns0:hi> but he had prayed for them, only they must also <ns0:hi>Watch</ns0:hi> and take heed, that they might not be Cheated, and deceived by them; tho they came with never so fair Pretences, for his com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing would be quite of another Nature, and his Kingdom, would be a quite other Kingdom.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west: so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 For wheresoever the carcass is, there will the eagles be gathered together.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath much the same<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Luk</ns0:hi> 17.24, 37. The Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />agreement of Interpreters, about the <ns0:hi>Coming</ns0:hi> of the Son of Man, here spoken of, makes a Variety in their Interpretation of these Verses. Some think the coming of the Son of Man here spoken of, was his coming to <ns0:hi>destroy Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> which he saith, will be sudden like the <ns0:hi>Lightning,</ns0:hi> which tho the Thunder be taken notice aforehand, as following the Light<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning, yet is not taken notice of. These Interpreters make the <ns0:hi>Carcass</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28. to be the Body of the <ns0:hi>Iewish Nation,</ns0:hi> designed to be destroyed, and the <ns0:hi>Eagles</ns0:hi> to be the <ns0:hi>Roman Armies. Iob</ns0:hi> saith of the <ns0:hi>Eagle Ch.</ns0:hi> 39. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 30. <ns0:hi>Where the slain are, there is she, Habbakuk, Ch.</ns0:hi> 1.8. saith the same of the <ns0:hi>Caldean Armies. They shall fly as the Eagle that hasteth to E<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>t.</ns0:hi> Some understand by the <ns0:hi>Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing of Christ</ns0:hi> here, his coming <ns0:hi>in his Spiritual Kingdom.</ns0:hi> The preaching of the Gospel shall be, <ns0:hi>like the Lightning</ns0:hi>; you need not listen after those that say: <ns0:hi>Lo here is Christ,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Lo he is there,</ns0:hi> for my Gospel shall be preached every where, and <ns0:hi>where the Carkass is,</ns0:hi> where my Death, and Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />surrection shall be preached, all the <ns0:hi>Elect, My sheep that hear my Voyce and follow me,</ns0:hi> shall be gathered together. Others understand it of Christ's coming to <ns0:hi>Iudgment,</ns0:hi> which is compared to <ns0:hi>Lightning</ns0:hi> for the suddenness, and <ns0:hi>Vniversality</ns0:hi> of it. There saith Christ I shall be, and all my Saints shall be gathered together, <ns0:hi>Luk<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> seemeth to speak of this, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 17.24.37. That Phrase, <ns0:hi>Wheresoever the Carcass is, there will the Eagles be gathered together,</ns0:hi> is a <ns0:hi>Proverbial Speech</ns0:hi> signifying, That it will need no great Labour to bring things together, which are naturally joyned by an innate Desire, either of them to the other; so that it is applicable in more Cases than one, and whether that Discourse in <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> were at the same time, when this was, I cannot say; our Saviours Discourse on this Argument, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 21. hath not these Verses, and is a part of a Discourse which <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 17. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 20. is said to have been be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gun at least to the <ns0:hi>Pharisees.</ns0:hi> But I shall further consider what <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, when I shall come to that Chapter in him.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Immediately after the tribula<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>ion of those days <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Joel 3.13. Act. 2.2<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.24. <ns0:hi>In those days after that Tribu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lation, the Sun shall be darkned, and the Moon shall not give her Light, and the Stars of Heaven shall fall, and the Powers that are in Heaven shall be shaken, Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.25. <ns0:hi>And there shall be signs in the Sun, and in the Moon, and in the Stars, and upon the Earth distress of Nations with Perplexity, the Sea and the Waves roaring: Mens Hearts failing them for Fear, and for looking after those things, which are coming on the Earth, for the Powers of Heaven shall be shaken.</ns0:hi> Interpreters are much divided in the Sense of these Words, whether they should be interpreted of <ns0:hi>Christs coming to the last Iudgment, and the signs of that:</ns0:hi> Or, 2. <ns0:hi>Concerning the Destruction of Ierusalem.</ns0:hi> Those who interpret it of the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> have the Context to guide them, as also the reports of Hi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />storians, of strange Prodigies seen in the Air, and Earth, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the taking of it; likewise the word <ns0:hi>Immediately after,</ns0:hi> &c. But I am more inclinable to interpret them of the <ns0:hi>last Iudgment,</ns0:hi> and to think that our Saviour is now passed to satisfie the Disciples about their other Question, concerning the end of the World, for altho, Christ's coming may sometimes signifie, that remarkable Act of his Providence, in the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction of his Enemies; yet the next Verses, speaking of his <ns0:hi>Coming with great Power and Glory,</ns0:hi> and of his <ns0:hi>Coming with his Angels, and with the sound of a Trumpet,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>gathering his Elect from the four Winds,</ns0:hi> the Phrases are so like the Phrases by which the Scripture expresseth Christ's coming to the last Judgment, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.52. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 4.16. and Christ speaking to his Disciples asking of him, as well about that, as the De<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem:</ns0:hi> I should rather interpret this Verse, with reference to the last Judgment, than the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> before spoken of, or at least, that these signs should be understood common both to the one, and the other; as divers of the other signs mentioned in this Chapter are. Some do think, that the darkening of the <ns0:hi>Sun</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Moon</ns0:hi> here, the <ns0:hi>falling of the Stars,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>shaking of the Powers of Heaven,</ns0:hi> are to be taken <ns0:hi>Metaphorically,</ns0:hi> as signifying the great Change should be in the <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Civil state</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> and it is true, that such kind of Expressions, do often in Scripture so signifie, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 13.10. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 24.23. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 32.7. <ns0:hi>Ioel</ns0:hi> 2.31. But without doubt the litteral Sense is not to be excluded, whether we understand the Text of the <ns0:hi>Destruction of Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> or of his coming to his last Judg<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, for, as Historians tell of great Prodigies seen before the former, so the Apostle confirms us, that there will be such things seen before the day of Judgment, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.10.12.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven, and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Rev. 1.7.</ns0:note> they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 13.41.</ns0:note> And he shall send his angels with a great <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Trumpet, <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> a great <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gether his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.26.27. <ns0:hi>And then shall they see the Son of Man, coming in the Clouds with great Power and Glory. And then shall he send his Angels, and shall gather together his Elect from the four Winds, from the utter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />most part of the Earth, to the uttermost part of Heaven. Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.27. <ns0:hi>And then they shall see the Son of Man, coming in a Cloud with great Power and Glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your Heads, for your Redemption draweth nigh.</ns0:hi> In<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />terpreters are also divided about these Words, as about the former, some understanding them concerning the <ns0:hi>Destruction of Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and Judging that by the <ns0:hi>sign of the coming of the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> is probably meant some <ns0:hi>Prodigy,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>some Comet</ns0:hi> seen before that Destruction, which should be of that Nature as it should make the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> (here called the <ns0:hi>Tribes of the Earth</ns0:hi>) to mourn, they by the <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> and Trumpet mentioned, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 31. understanding the Ministers of the Gospel, who after the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> should go and preach the Gospel over all the World, and so gather in the Elect into the Gospel-Church. But I cannot agree this Sense, and I said the most Interpreters expound these Words of the last Judgment; what is meant by <ns0:hi>the sign of the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> all are not so well agreed, two of the Evangelists say only <ns0:hi>the Son of Man: Matthew</ns0:hi> mentions, first the appearance of the <ns0:hi>sign of the Son of Man,</ns0:hi> then the <ns0:hi>Son of Man</ns0:hi> himself, pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bably it signifieth some great Prodigy, that shall be seen be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore that great and Terrible day. Those things which incline me to think, that the day of Judgment, not the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rusalem,</ns0:hi> is that which is spoken of in these Verses, is, 1. That all the Phrases are such as the Scripture useth, to express Christ's coming to the last Judgment. <ns0:hi>His coming in the Clouds of Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, Math.</ns0:hi> 26.64. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.7. the <ns0:hi>Tribes of the Earth mourning, Rev.</ns0:hi> 1.7. his <ns0:hi>coming</ns0:hi> with the <ns0:hi>Angels,</ns0:hi> and the sound of a <ns0:hi>Trum<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pet. Math.</ns0:hi> 25.31. <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 8.38. 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 15.52. 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 4.16. His sending his Angels to <ns0:hi>gather the Elect, Mat.</ns0:hi> 13.49. 2. <ns0:hi>The Tribes of the Earth mourning,</ns0:hi> seems to signifie more then the twelve Tribes of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> 3. That which <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath, <ns0:hi>Look up, and lift up your Heads, for the day of your Redemption draweth nigh</ns0:hi>; seemeth hardly applicable to the <ns0:hi>Destruction of Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> rather to the <ns0:hi>Redemption of the Body</ns0:hi> mentioned, <ns0:hi>Rom.</ns0:hi> 8.23. For the Gospel before this time was carried to the <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi>: Nor do I know, that that is any where called <ns0:hi>Redemption.</ns0:hi> Those things which have led some learned Interpreters to expound, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29, 30, 31. of the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> are, I conceive, those Particles, <ns0:hi>Immediately</ns0:hi> after the <ns0:hi>Tribulation of those days, v.</ns0:hi> 29. and the Particle <ns0:hi>then, v.</ns0:hi> 30. together with <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 34. where our Saviour saith: <ns0:hi>This Generation shall not <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> till all these things be fulfilled.</ns0:hi> But the term <ns0:hi>Immediately</ns0:hi> after the Tribulation of those days, may signifie not only the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> but that and all the Calamities of those days, that should follow that, to the end of the World: And it is very usual for Prophetical Scriptures to speak of things to come long after, as if they were presently to come to pass, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 32.35. and the <ns0:hi>day of Iudgment</ns0:hi> is ordinarily spoken of, as if it were at hand, 1 <ns0:hi>Thes.</ns0:hi> 4.15. <ns0:hi>Ia.</ns0:hi> 5.8. 1 <ns0:hi>Ioh.</ns0:hi> 2.18. both to denote the <ns0:hi>certainty</ns0:hi> of it, and to keep us from Security, and to let us know that a Thousand years in Gods sight, are but as one day, 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.8. for the 34. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> we shall give the Sence of it in its Order.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:264" />32 Now learn a parable of the fig-tree, When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> nigh.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Jam. 5.9.</ns0:note> that it is near, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> at the doors.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="34">34 Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 102.26. Isa. 51.6. Chap. 5.18. Heb. 1.11.</ns0:note> Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> hath the very same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 28, 29, 30, 31. So hath <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 21. <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 29, 30, 31, 32, 33. only he saith, the <ns0:hi>Fig-tree and all Trees, when they now shoot forth, you see, and know of your own selves, that Summer is nigh at hand. So ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know you that the Kingdom of God is nigh at hand</ns0:hi>: Verily, &c. By this Similitude of the <ns0:hi>Fig-tree</ns0:hi> (called therefore by <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> a <ns0:hi>Parable</ns0:hi>) Our Saviour doth not only design to inform them, that these things which he had told them, should be as certain signs of the approaching of the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and the coming of his Kingdom, as the Fig-trees, and other Trees putting forth of leaves, is a sign of the approaching Summer, as <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 2.13. but that as the Frosts, and Snow, and Cold of the Winter, doth not hinder the Trees from bringing forth Fruit in the Summer, so these <ns0:hi>Tribulations</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Troubles</ns0:hi> should be so far from hindring, and de<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>troying Christ's Kingdom, that they should prepare the World <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>or it, and promove it; so that as they might know from these Tribulations in <ns0:hi>I<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>dea,</ns0:hi> that the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Grace</ns0:hi> was at hand, and began: So from the following Tribula<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tions upon the World, they might know that his Kingdom of Glory was also hastening. <ns0:hi>Verily I say unto you, this Genera<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.</ns0:hi> There are several Notions men have of that term. <ns0:hi>This Generation,</ns0:hi> some by it understanding mankind, others, The Generation of <ns0:hi>Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans,</ns0:hi> Others the whole Generation of the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; but doubtless our Saviour means the <ns0:hi>Set of Men that were at that time in the World:</ns0:hi> Those who were at that time living should not all dye, <ns0:hi>until all these things shall be fulfilled,</ns0:hi> all that he had spo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ken with reference <ns0:hi>to the Destruction of Ierusalem</ns0:hi>; and indeed the most of those signs, which our Saviour gave were signs common, both to the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and the last Judgment, abating only Christ's personal coming in the Clouds, with Power and Glory. So that considering, that the Destructi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> was within less than forty years after our Saviour's speaking these words, so many as lived to the Expira<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion of that number of years, must see the far greater part of these things actually fulfilled, as signs of the Destruction of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>fulfilling,</ns0:hi> as signs of the end of the World. <ns0:hi>Heaven and Earth shall pass away, but my Words shall not pass away.</ns0:hi> By this Expression our Saviour confirmeth the Truth of what he had said, assuring those to whom he spake: That altho there should be a change of the <ns0:hi>Heavens,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Earth,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.10.12, 13. which Men commonly look upon as the most stable, and abiding things, yet the Truth of what he had said should not fail.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no not the angels of heaven, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zech. 14.7.</ns0:note> but my Father only.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> addeth, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.32. <ns0:hi>Neither the Son, but the Father,</ns0:hi> of that <ns0:hi>Day</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hour,</ns0:hi> that is, the particular time when the <ns0:hi>Heavens and the Earth shall pass away,</ns0:hi> as he had before said, or when the <ns0:hi>End of the World shall be,</ns0:hi> which was one of the <ns0:hi>Questions</ns0:hi> propounded to him by his Disciples, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 3. knoweth no Man, no meer Man, nor have Men any reason to be troubled at it; for it is a piece of Knowledge, which the <ns0:hi>Father</ns0:hi> hath re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />served into his own Power, and his own Pleasure, from the <ns0:hi>An<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gels,</ns0:hi> who continually behold his Face. Nay I my self as <ns0:hi>M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>n</ns0:hi> know it not, nor is it more absurd, or derogating from the Perfection of Christ, then for to say, that Christ as Man, was not <ns0:hi>Omnipotent,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Omniscient,</ns0:hi> &c. By the way this gives a great Check, to the Curiosity of Mens inquiries after the particular time, or year when t<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e World shall have an end, or the day of Judgment begin, or be.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 But as the days of Noe <ns0:hi>were,</ns0:hi> so also shall the coming of the son of man be.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 For as in the days that were before the flood, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 7.5.</ns0:note> they were eating and drinking, marrying and gi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ving in marriage, until the day that Noe entred in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />to the ark,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath much the same, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 17.26, 27. where he also saith, it shall be as in the days of <ns0:hi>Lot,</ns0:hi> but I shall consider what he saith, w<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ich seemeth spo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>en at another time, and upon another oc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />casion; when I come to his seventeenth Chapter. Two things our Saviour see<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eth here to teach us. 1. <ns0:hi>That Christ's coming to the last Iudgmen<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> will be sudden,</ns0:hi> and not <ns0:hi>lookt for</ns0:hi>; upon which Account his coming is compared in Scripture to the coming of a Thief, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 43.44. 2 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 3.10. <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 16.15. 2. That it will be <ns0:hi>in a <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ime of great Security, and Deba<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>chery,</ns0:hi> such was the time of <ns0:hi>Noah, Gen.</ns0:hi> 6.3, 4, 5.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="40">40 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 17.36.</ns0:note> Then shall two be in the field, the one shall be taken, and the other left.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="41">41 Two <ns0:hi>women shall</ns0:hi> be grinding at the mill, the one shall be taken, and the other left.<ns0:note place="bottom">Some refer this, to the coming of Christ in his Kingdom of Grace, some to his coming in the day of Judgment, it is true of both those comings. God shews the freeness of his Grace much in the Conversion of sinners, and makes Discriminations of which we can give no Account, as he tells us, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 4.25, 26, 27, 28. but it seemeth here rather to be understood of that Sepa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration, which Christ shall make at the day of Judgment, <ns0:hi>of the Sheep from the Goats,</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Elect</ns0:hi> from the <ns0:hi>Reprobates</ns0:hi>; for of that coming our Saviour seemeth to be speaking, both in the preceeding, and in the following Words.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="42">42 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 25.13.</ns0:note> Watch therefore, for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="43">43 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 12.39. 1 Thes. 5.2. 2 Pet. 3.10. Rev. 3.3. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 16.15.</ns0:note> But know this, That if the good man of the house had known, in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="44">44 Therefore be ye also ready, for in such an hour as you think not, the son of man cometh.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Take you heed, Watch and Pray, for you know not when the time is, Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.33. what our Lord here meaneth by <ns0:hi>Watching</ns0:hi> is easily gathered, as well by what went before, where our Saviour had been speaking of the <ns0:hi>Security</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luxury</ns0:hi> of the old World: As by what followeth, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 44. where he biddeth them, <ns0:hi>be always ready,</ns0:hi> and therefore <ns0:hi>Luke, Ch.</ns0:hi> 21.34. ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pounds this thus: <ns0:hi>And take heed to your selves, lest at any time your Hearts be over-charged with Su<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>fetting, and Drunkenness, and Cares of this Life, and so that day come upon you at un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />awares. For as a snare shall it come on all them, that dwell on the Face of the whole Earth. Watch you therefore and Pray, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things, that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of Man.</ns0:hi> Our Saviour in these Verses, from the incertainty of the particular time, when the day of Judgment shall be, presseth up<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on his Disciples, a <ns0:hi>Sober, Heavenly</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Holy Life</ns0:hi>; intimating that by such a Life only, they can make themselves ready for the coming of Christ, and to <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tand before the Son of Man, when he shall appear in his Power and Glory. He presseth this from that which common Prudence would teach any Housholder viz. If he knew in what Watch of the Night a Thief would come to watch, and not suffer his House to be broken open. That is, in what time of the Night, (<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 
                     <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> divided the Night into the <ns0:hi>first, second, third,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>fourth Watch,</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Romans</ns0:hi> di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vided it for relief of their Military Guards. Now (saith our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour) you, knowing that there will come such a time, and not certainly knowing at what time, stand concerned to be always Watching and Praying.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="45">45 Who then is a faithful, and wise servant, whom his Lord hath made ruler over his houshold to give them meat in due season?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="46">46 Blessed <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> that servant, whom his Lord when he cometh shall find so doing.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="47">47 Verily I say unto you, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 25.21<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>23.</ns0:note> that he shall make him ruler over all his goods.<ns0:note place="bottom">We have much the same, <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> 12, 41, 42, 43. whether spake at the sa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>e time, and upo<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the same occasion or no I know n<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t. It is said there, <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 41. That <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> gave occasion to this Disco<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>rse by saying<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Lord speakest thou this Parable to us, or even to all</ns0:hi>? Our Saviour replyeth as here, only <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> saith, <ns0:hi>Who is that Faithful and Wise Steward</ns0:hi>? The Question intimates that there are but a few such. This Discourse plainly referreth to the Ministers of the Gospel, whom Christ leaveth in trust with his Church, to <ns0:hi>give them their Meat in due Season,</ns0:hi> he decl<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>reth the Blessedness of those Ministers that shall be found Faithfully discharging their Trust, and that the Lord in the Day of Judgment will exalt them to a much greater Honour, ac<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cording to that of <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 12.3. <ns0:hi>They that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the Firmament: and they that turn many to Righteousness, as the Stars for ever and ever.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="48">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:265" />48 But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My Lord delayeth his coming.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="49">49 And shall begin to smite <ns0:hi>his</ns0:hi> fellow servants, and to eat, and drink with the drunken.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="50">50 The Lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>cut him off.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> And shall cut him asunder, and appoint <ns0:hi>him</ns0:hi> his portion with the hypocrites, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 8.12.</ns0:note> there shall be weep<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, and gnashing of teeth.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> hath much of this, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 12.45. <ns0:hi>But and if that Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vant say in his Heart, my Lord delayeth his coming, and shall begin to beat the Men-servants and Maid-servants, and to Eat, and Drink and to be Drunken. The Lord of that Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />v<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>nt will come in a Day when he looketh not for him, and at an Hour when he is not aware, and will appoint him his Por<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion with unbelievers.</ns0:hi> If that Servant prove an Evil Servant, presumeth upon my not making such hast to Judgment, as he thought I would, and shall prove a Persecutor of my People, or a loose and Debauched Person, I will come to his particular Judg<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent before I come to the General Judgment, and at such a time as he shall not be aware of me, and destroy him, an<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> give him his Portion with such as believe not my second coming, and with such as are one thing in Profession, and ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther thing in Practice, in Hell where the Condition of poor Crea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tures will be Miserable, as the Condition of those that Weep and G<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ash their Teeth. By this Parable our Savi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ur d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th qui<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ken his Apostles, to whom he intended to leave the care of his Church, when he should be ascended into Heaven, to a faithful care of the Flock committed to their Trust, & also lets us know that in succeed<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing Ages, there would arise a Generation, of loose, and debauched Ministers, and such as would persecute the sincerer Professors of his Gospel, who could not comply with their Doctrines, and Lives. Of which as all Ages of the Church have given a proof: So the time since <ns0:hi>Popery</ns0:hi> hath prevailed in the World, hath given a more plentiful, and abundant proof. All which Extravagan<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cies are incouraged from their <ns0:hi>Atheisme,</ns0:hi> and unbelief of Christs coming to Judgment. He also sheweth how severe he will be a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst such Persons. He will come upon them before they be aware of it, and <ns0:hi>Cut them in pieces.</ns0:hi> The Word signifies to cut them in two Pieces, as the Jews were wont to divide their Sacri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fices: or (as some think) as some Pagan Nations were wont to punish perfidious Persons, and some more Notorious Malefa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ctors, and give him his Portion with unbelievers, and Hypocrites in Hell, <ns0:hi>Ch.</ns0:hi> 13.42. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 25.30. The Case of all Persons that live securely, and debauched Lives, because Judgment is not spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ly Executed, will be sad: but the Case of Ministers that do so will be dre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>d<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ul. They are a sort of Sinners, whom God seldom suffereth to live out half their Days: and when he doth, yet they shall not escape the severe<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t Damnation of Hell. They be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tray a greater trust, and lead Multitudes to Hell with them, and so are the greatest <ns0:hi>Traytors</ns0:hi> against the <ns0:hi>Divine Majesty.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
